scenarios.name: DB outage
scenarios.hypothesis: With Postgres paused, /course fails fast with a clean 5xx (no traceback), / stays 200, and the app recovers automatically on unpause.

steps.name: degrade — data route fails fast
steps.expectation: /course returns a clean 5xx within timeout, no leaked traceback

steps.name: partial availability — static route
steps.expectation: / stays 200 while the DB is down (graceful degradation, not total outage)

steps.name: auto-recovery
steps.expectation: /course returns to 200 within 30s of unpause, no manual restart

scenarios.name: Process kill
scenarios.hypothesis: When the web process dies, the restart policy returns /course to 200 with no manual intervention (RestartCount increments), and data reads stay consistent.

steps.name: auto-restart recovery
steps.expectation: restart policy returns /course to 200 within 60s, no manual intervention

steps.name: restart policy engaged
steps.expectation: container RestartCount increments — recovery was the policy, not a coincidence

steps.name: clean DB reconnect
steps.expectation: data route serves consistent data after restart (pool re-established)

scenarios.name: DB latency (grey failure)
scenarios.hypothesis: With ~600ms injected on the DB path, /course stays 200 (correctness preserved) but breaches the 500ms p95 SLO, the breach is visible in Prometheus, and latency returns to baseline on removal.

steps.name: steady state
steps.expectation: /course == 200 and under the 500ms SLO before fault

steps.name: graceful degradation under latency
steps.expectation: /course still 200 but slower than the 500ms SLO (degrades, not breaks)

steps.name: SLO breach observed (Prometheus)
steps.expectation: the injected latency breaches the p95 SLO panel — the observability stack catches the grey failure

steps.name: recovery
steps.expectation: /course returns to 200 under the 500ms SLO once the toxic is removed
